title: Confident, Not Correct
description: Tay trusts the shop bot. Ms. Odette shows why AI can sound sure and still be wrong. The story is fiction; the facts are sourced: anthropic.com/research/tracing-thoughts-language-model and Claude's docs on reducing hallucinations. Illustrated still scenes, one narrator voice.

scenes.speaker: tay
scenes.caption: "BOLT said it, so it's facts."
scenes.narration: Tay swears the shop bot is never wrong.

scenes.speaker: reggie
scenes.caption: Sure ain't the same as right.
scenes.narration: "It sounded so sure, Unc." Uncle Reggie laughs. "Sure ain't the same as right."

scenes.speaker: odette
scenes.caption: AI writes one word at a time, always guessing the next.
scenes.narration: At the chalkboard, Ms. Odette explains. AI models are trained to write one word at a time, always guessing the next word. So an answer can sound right and still be untrue.

scenes.speaker: nia
scenes.caption: Like autocomplete: it finishes the sentence, true or not.
scenes.narration: "Think autocomplete," says Nia. "It finishes your sentence, true or not."

scenes.speaker: nia
scenes.caption: Let it say "I don't know." Ask for sources. Check them.
scenes.narration: "So let it say I don't know, and ask for sources. Then check them." Reggie nods. "Trust, then verify."

scenes.speaker: bolt
scenes.caption: Next: BOLT vs. Ms. Odette. Follow for part 2.
scenes.narration: "I am one hundred percent sure," says BOLT. Part two, next time.
